source.title: Performance-Carbon Trade-Offs across Architectural Biases in Shear Flow Forecasting
source.authors: Sophia N. Wilson; J. Christensen; Raghavendra Selvan

record.tranche_reason: Compares architectural biases and reports forecasting performance under several model settings, providing conceptual evidence about architecture and generalization on natural data, though it does not test the claim's specific classification or training-test error-gap measures.
record.gate_note: Reports rollout forecast metrics by architecture, receptive field, and periodicity; these are relevant to V3. It does not report arbitrary-label fitting, training-versus-test error gaps, or measured network properties tracking those gaps. No rows for carbon/runtime findings because they do not measure the claim's generalization outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study compares convolutional architectures and Fourier neural operators on shear-flow forecasting, without a fully connected comparator. It therefore does not test V3's convolutional-versus-fully-connected image generalization claim. Its other experiments do not test any remaining version; using AdamW is not an optimizer comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the predictive-performance findings and the authors' tentative attribution of UFNO's advantage to its multiscale structure, but omits their main conclusion: model evaluation should account for predictive performance and carbon costs across training and inference. No model dominates all three, and runtime is an imperfect proxy for carbon cost. The authors restrict their findings to the tested PDE, dataset subset, model families, and hardware.
record.recipe_differences: Autoregressive spatio-temporal PDE forecasting evaluation with rollout accuracy and physics-fidelity metrics, not image classification held-out error or a train-test gap measure.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture and evaluation metric; rollout performance changes across model families and padding variants.

fits_no_version.finding: UNet-CN outperforms UNet; circular padding improves UNet and has mixed benefits for UNet-CN; FNO and TFNO perform relatively poorly, while UFNO leads across the four rollout metrics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture and periodic boundary assumptions affect held-out autoregressive shear-flow forecasting performance, with benefits depending on the backbone and evaluation metric.

record.problems: Results are limited to one PDE system, dataset subset, model families, and GPU. Rollout metrics are mostly presented in figures without exact values in text. Performance is evaluated during autoregressive rollout, while models were trained on one-step prediction. No direct training-test generalization gap is measured.
record.rows_left_out: No results were omitted; carbon emissions, runtime, and the introductory PINN toy experiment do not measure the generalization outcomes specified in the claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting alongside natural-label and random-label held-out performance.
Test-error trends when widening networks beyond the width required for zero training error.

All parts: convolutional versus fully connected image-network performance, the contribution of local connectivity, learned sparse local connections, and initialization from trained convolutional networks.
Adaptive-versus-SGD generalization comparisons and the effects of tuning, decoupled weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations that reduce their penalty.
Dropout effects on held-out error, including training-set size, dropout strength, and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with generalization gaps and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Forecasting on held-out trajectories is a generalization evaluation, but does not by itself test one of the specified versions. Global receptive field is not equivalent to a fully connected architecture. The record's V3 limits_scope label should be removed.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweep beyond interpolation threshold and test-error trend.
Fully connected image classifiers, standard gradient training comparison, sparse local connections, and convolutional initialization transfer.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out comparison.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparison to other gap measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: UNet
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated autoregressive forecasting in a 50-step rollout.
rows.measure: VRMSE, Pearson r, velocity divergence, and spectral energy error across rollout steps
rows.note: Rollout metrics are shown graphically; the text provides comparative descriptions but no exact values.
rows.check: UNet rollout metrics do not establish any claim version; there is no fully connected comparator. The four measures should be separate rows if retained.

rows.subject: UNet-CN
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated autoregressive forecasting in a 50-step rollout.

conditions.value: local receptive field, zero-padded; ConvNeXt variant

rows.measure: VRMSE, Pearson r, velocity divergence, and spectral energy error across rollout steps
rows.value: Outperforms UNet by a wide margin across all evaluation metrics.
rows.note: Text gives a direct qualitative comparison; exact metric values are figure-only.
rows.check: The reported improvement compares two convolutional architectures, not convolutional and fully connected networks. The qualitative value matches the text, but cannot establish V3. Four measures are bundled.

rows.subject: UNet-CP
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated autoregressive forecasting in a 50-step rollout.
rows.measure: VRMSE, Pearson r, velocity divergence, and spectral energy error across rollout steps
rows.value: Circular padding improves all four metrics for UNet.
rows.note: Qualitative comparison; exact metric values are figure-only.
rows.check: The reported improvement tests circular versus zero padding within UNet, not V3's architectural comparison. The qualitative value matches the text. Four measures are bundled.

rows.subject: UNet-CN-CP
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated autoregressive forecasting in a 50-step rollout.

conditions.value: local receptive field; ConvNeXt variant with circular padding

rows.measure: VRMSE, Pearson r, velocity divergence, and spectral energy error across rollout steps
rows.value: Circular padding improves or leaves roughly unchanged three of four metrics; spectral energy error is the exception.
rows.note: The described effect is not uniform across metrics; exact values are figure-only.
rows.check: The padding comparison does not test any version. The text supports improvement or little change on three metrics, with spectral energy error the exception; this is not partial evidence for V3. Four measures are bundled.

rows.subject: FNO
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated autoregressive forecasting in a 50-step rollout.
rows.measure: VRMSE, Pearson r, velocity divergence, and spectral energy error across rollout steps
rows.baseline: Other evaluated models, not individually stated
rows.value: FNO and TFNO perform relatively poorly on all four metrics.
rows.note: The comparison is jointly stated for FNO and TFNO; exact values are figure-only.
rows.check: FNO is a Fourier neural operator, not the fully connected image-network comparator named by V3. Relatively poor rollout performance does not constitute partial evidence for that version. Four measures are bundled.

rows.subject: UFNO
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated autoregressive forecasting in a 50-step rollout.

conditions.value: global receptive field; Fourier representation and U-shaped variant

rows.measure: VRMSE, Pearson r, velocity divergence, and spectral energy error across rollout steps
rows.baseline: Other evaluated models, not individually stated
rows.value: Performs best across all four metrics; performs well across pointwise accuracy and physics-fidelity metrics for most of the rollout.
rows.note: Text identifies UFNO as best across four metrics, while noting this holds for most of the rollout.
rows.check: UFNO's leading rollout performance does not test convolutional versus fully connected image networks. The qualitative value matches the text, but cannot establish V3. Four measures are bundled.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Shear-flow forecasting models in the tested family and 50-step rollout
reader_labels.reason: Results differ by architecture and metric: UNet-CN improves over UNet, padding's effect varies by backbone and metric, and the global-receptive-field FNO variants do not uniformly outperform; UFNO performs best, which the authors associate with its multi-scale structure (R2–R7).
